$comment: PR review risk tiering. Read by ~/.claude/hooks/pr-review-policy.sh.
Any file matching 'high' => HIGH (Gitar + CodeRabbit). All files matching 'low' => LOW.
Everything else => NORMAL (Gitar only). No match anywhere => NORMAL, deliberately.
.gitignore is deliberately NOT high, and must not be re-added without first removing
the CI guard that replaced it. It was high because re-excluding .claude/ deletes this
file, and a repo with no policy tiers every PR NORMAL - the one edit that can disable
review everywhere would have got the lighter review. But tiering is path-glob only, so
it could not tell that edit apart from ignoring a scratch directory, and every trivial
ignore change billed a scarce CodeRabbit review. ci.yml now asserts the invariant
directly (this file tracked and unignored), which is deterministic and free where a
reviewer noticing was neither. Gitar still reviews .gitignore at NORMAL.
HIGH covers deploy/ (this repo has a real deploy target).
LOW justification for THIS repo: docs/ is developer documentation with no site build.
src/ contains the CI dashboard's JobLanes configuration, which the scaffold-ci job
naming contract depends on - that is NORMAL, never low.
Dependency manifests are deliberately NOT in 'high' and must not be added (estate rule,
2026-07-29) - package.json, package-lock.json, Directory.Packages.props, **/*.csproj. They are
what Dependabot edits, and dependency PRs are out of AI code review on both vendors:
CodeRabbit refuses bot authors outright and Gitar's bot review is switched off, because
reviewing every bump exhausts the allowance and starves the changes that need it. Listing
them HIGH would demand a reviewer that can never run - coverage on paper, none in fact. CI
plus Dependabot's own advisory data is what gates a bump. nuget.config, global.json
and Directory.Build.props stay HIGH: registry/feed, SDK-pin and analyzer config, not bot-edited.
